definition: Of or relating to rain or rainfall; concerned with the distribution or measurement of precipitation.
etymology: From Greek hyetos, meaning rain, itself from hyein, to rain — the same root that gives us Hyades, the cluster of stars whose rising the ancient Greeks believed brought the rainy season. The word traveled into English through scientific Latin in the nineteenth century, when meteorology was busy naming everything it could measure.
usage: Hyetal maps charting the wet and dry belts of a continent have a quiet beauty to them, all those gradient washes of blue deepening toward the monsoon coasts.
